deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It continues Riemann's excerpt or paraphrase of J. F. Herbart's 'Allgemeine Metaphysik', Einleitung, Cap. VI, §. 211, on the relation of metaphysics to the other philosophical sciences. The previous page breaks off in the same paragraph, at 'daraus wurden die Prinzipien alles Denkens und Erkennens des Kantia[nismus]'. The next page moves on to excerpts from Herbart's 'Psychologie als Wissenschaft' (Werke Bd. VI) and the 'Lehrbuch zur Psychologie' (Bd. V).

The argument, step by step:
(1) A false psychology would claim dominion, but it 'nimmermehr mächtig werden' (could never become powerful) and would have to be merely tolerated.
(2) Neither metaphysics nor psychology simply 'gives' the basic concepts (Grundbegriffe). The 'prejudice of the categories' is the view that concepts once present in the human mind are fixed and must be used as they are. The history of philosophy refutes it, since concepts have undergone manifold transformations (Umwandlungen).
(3) Even before science, common understanding confronted the empirical concept of change (Veränderung) and its inner contradiction. It invented, as a necessary remedy, the causal (or inherence) concept. This was a transformation left 'auf halbem Wege'.
(4) Metaphysics continues this work and transforms further concepts. Until the work is finished it splits into rival systems, which give no rest until it is done.
(5) Psychology, cut off from metaphysics, oversteps its domain. It knows only the manifestations and inner appearances of the soul (Geist und Gemüth). It may collect experiences and should learn the causal relations among representations (Vorstellungen). It knows nothing of attractive and repulsive forces, of the connection of substance with will, or of how bodily changes can produce a representation in the soul.
(6) If psychology claims to resolve these riddles, it has thereby discovered its kinship (Verwandtschaft, replacing a struck 'Abhängigkeit') with metaphysics and acknowledged its dependence on it.

Relevance for Riemann: this belongs to his Herbart studies, the background of his own 'Naturphilosophie' fragments. The themes include psychology founded on causal relations among Vorstellungen, attraction and repulsion, and soul–body interaction. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Excerpt/paraphrase of Herbart's view that basic concepts (categories) are not fixed but are historically transformed by metaphysics, and that psychology depends on metaphysics
Riemann's documented reading of Herbart as background to his Naturphilosophie fragments
results.modern_name: Herbart's influence on Riemann (noted by Riemann himself: 'Der Verfasser ist Herbartianer in Psychologie und Erkenntnisstheorie')
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (well-known; discussed by Scholz, Ferreirós, Bottazzini, Pulte and others)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely philosophical excerpt from Herbart's Allgemeine Metaphysik, with no mathematics. Riemann's study of Herbart is well documented and discussed in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2–3: the image suggests 'als ob die Begriffe ... ein für allemal im menschlichen Geiste wäre[n], und müssten unabänderlich so bleiben, und so gebraucht werden, wie sie einmal sind' rather than 'die einmal im menschlichen Geiste wohnen, unveränderlich so bleiben'.
Line 7: 'erfahrungsmässig' is underlined in the manuscript; so are 'allen' and the word after 'ungeheures[?]' (possibly 'gemeinschaftliches' rather than 'gewöhnlich') in line 8.

Line 9: 'die Inhärenzbegriff' is more plausibly 'den Causalbegriff'. The parallel passage on the previous page reads 'Widerspruch in der Veränderung, welchen schon der gemeine Verstand das natürliche Heilmittel des Causalbegriffs erfindet', and Herbart's §211 has the causal concept as remedy for the contradiction of change.
Line 9: 'sich losgerissen / so hat sich' — the manuscript reads roughly '— sich losgerissen [?], und hat sich ...'; the sentence is garbled in both readings.
Line 23: 'das Causalverhältniss der Vorstellungen unter einander mag und sollte sie kennen lernen' is underlined in the manuscript (the underline runs onto the next line).
Final line: 'anerkannt' is underlined; 'Abhängigkeit' is struck in the preceding line and replaced by 'Verwandtschaft', as transcribed.
